narrative:
At a Hollow Reaches roadside inn, Elder Pella coughs once into a handkerchief and apologizes for the noise. Her grandson keeps pouring tea as though politeness can hold the room together. Old Hendrik sits near the stove, quieter than you remember.

@Hendrik: Weather gets into old beams. And old lungs. Don't look at me like that.

narrative:
Bettina unlocks the medicine chest exactly once. There is enough for one household. Hendrik's room is at one end of the lane; a family of strangers burns with fever at the other. A merchant offers more gold than the whole village has seen this year.

@Bettina: Procedure has no answer for this. It only says I must write down what you decide.

narrative: The cordon holds, barely. Yssa sleeps sitting upright for the first time in weeks. If Hendrik lives, he complains that everyone has become too gentle with him; if he does not, his empty chair remains near the stove. The village learns the names of the dead before it learns to laugh again.

narrative: The cordon breaks where hunger always breaks it: at a family door. Carts leave for the Capital before the fever has finished choosing them. Bettina records each departure and then tears the page from her ledger.

narrative: A royal carriage passes the Hollow road under black curtains. The King is ill, the driver says, and the Capital has begun to count heirs aloud. The plague has reached farther than any cart, even where no fever followed.
